summary_for_children: Al-Fatihah is the prayer we say in every salah. We praise Allah, remember His mercy, and ask Him to guide us on the straight path.
environment_concept: A symbolic path (Al-Fatihah has no story): a gate of praise hung with flowers (1:2), a garden of mercy where dry beds bloom when watered (1:3, with 30:50), a terrace facing a wide dawn horizon (1:4; nothing of the Day is pictured) and a fork where one bright road runs straight (1:6).
architecture_and_scenery: Low arches of pale stone, a walled garden with a central fountain, and a long straight walkway lit at dawn.

palette.lighting: Low golden sunrise, long soft shadows
palette.atmosphere: Clear and calm, light mist over the garden

areas.name: Gate of Praise
areas.description: An arch where the walk begins; reading 1:2 lights the gateway.

areas.name: Garden of Mercy
areas.description: A walled garden whose fountain flows when 1:3 is read.

areas.name: Horizon of Recompense
areas.description: A distant, quiet horizon line: symbolic only, nothing of the unseen is shown.

areas.name: Fork of the Straight Path
areas.description: Where the path divides; the straight road is lit, the others fade.

activities.name: Seven-step walk
activities.description: Carry seven numbered stepping stones, one for each ayah, and lay them in order along the straight road.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

activities.name: Asking for help
activities.description: A lantern the child lights by reading 1:5, linking worship and asking Allah for help.
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

activities.name: Bring the garden to life
activities.description: Carry water jars from the fountain to three dry beds; each one blooms. Linked to 30:50: "observe the effects of the mercy of Allah - how He gives life to the earth after its lifelessness". (30:50 is quoted as a related ayah from another surah.)
activities.label: artistic educational adaptation, not an event in the Quran

narration_plan: A gentle narrator explains each ayah's meaning at its stone, then pauses so the child can read the Arabic.
learning_objectives: Explain what we ask for in 1:6
Connect the surah to daily prayer

status.playable_environment: first version built: its own scene (gate, garden, terrace, fork) with two hands-on activities in the scene
status.testing: checked in headless Chromium with software WebGL at 960x600; not tested on phones or real GPUs
status.tested_by: automated screenshots of the scene and the in-scene activities

depiction_rules: No prophet, person or representation of Allah is shown. Unseen realities are never pictured. Interactive activities are labelled as adaptations.

adventure_world.title: The Seven Gates
adventure_world.source: "Quran Adventure: First 10 Unique Worlds" with the rule "114 unique game experiences" (2026-11-04); replaces the first adventure version built from the earlier design table
adventure_world.status: second version built for the web: each world now has its own core mechanic; draft, unreviewed; checked in headless Chromium with software WebGL only, not on phones or real GPUs
adventure_world.note: The new-look adventure world for this surah. It is a separate design from the composed scene this record describes; both are kept until reviewers choose.
adventure_world.core_play: An architectural journey: seven chambers in a row, each opened by a different small act (standing, looking, opening a spring, waiting, facing, finding the straight way), ending with the whole surah.

unique_world.visual_theme: Seven walled stone chambers on a sunrise terrace, cypress and fig, gold light

primary_mechanic.text: Seven chambers, one per ayah; each gate opens by a different act (stand at the threshold, find window points, open a spring, wait at a sundial, face a niche, find the way through a maze, read the whole surah).

secondary_activities: open the spring so a pool fills
unique_world.narrative_structure: Linear: seven rooms in ayah order, ending on a terrace reading 1:1-7
environment_behaviour: spring fills a pool and beds appear
unique_world.learning_objective: Know the seven ayahs of Al-Fatihah in order and what each asks of us
